speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe what your dizziness feels like—is it a spinning sensation or more like feeling faint?

Also, when did these symptoms first start, and have they been constant or do they come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the spinning sensation suggests vertigo. Given your recent garlic intake, could you tell me if you have noticed any garlic or onion odor in your breath or urine, or if the symptoms worsen significantly with head movements?
